metadata.note: 3m: define linear momentum + state SI unit. Cloze: 'product of [mass] and [velocity] / [vector] quantity / SI unit [kg m/s]'. Marks: 1+1+0.5+0.5. Note caribbean context: truck on Sir George Walter Highway is in Q4b (calculation), not this definition sub-part.

question.name: CSEC Phy Jan 2022 Q4a(i) — Define Linear Momentum and State SI Unit
question.text:
Define the term 'linear momentum' and state its SI unit by completing the statements below:

Linear momentum is the product of an object's [[1]] and its [[2]]. It is a [[3]] quantity. Its SI unit is [[4]].
question.general_feedback:
Linear momentum (p):

Linear momentum is the product of an object's mass and its velocity:

p = mv

It is a vector quantity — it has both magnitude and direction (in the direction of the velocity).

Its SI unit is kg m s⁻¹ (kilogram metre per second), also written as kg·m/s or N·s.

ddwtos.cloze_html: Linear momentum is the product of an object's [[1]] and its [[2]]. It is a [[3]] quantity. Its SI unit is [[4]].

groups.label: Linear momentum = ___ × velocity
groups.diagnostic_hint: Linear momentum = MASS × velocity (p = mv). Mass is the scalar quantity of matter; when multiplied by velocity (a vector) the result is a vector quantity.

groups.label: Linear momentum = mass × ___
groups.diagnostic_hint: Linear momentum = mass × VELOCITY (not speed — velocity is the vector, which is why momentum is also a vector). p = mv, units: kg m s⁻¹.

groups.label: Linear momentum is a ___ quantity
groups.diagnostic_hint: Linear momentum is a VECTOR quantity — it has both magnitude and direction. This is why "conservation of momentum" must account for direction (e.g., in collisions).

groups.label: SI unit of linear momentum
groups.diagnostic_hint: Unit = kg m s⁻¹ (kilogram metre per second). Alternative: N s (newton-second), since 1 N s = 1 kg m s⁻¹. NOT kg m s⁻² (that is the unit of force/newton).

ddwtos.word_bank_note: 15 tokens for 4 slots. Slot 1 (mass): 'weight' is a common confusion — weight is a force (N), not mass. 'density' is mass per unit volume. 'acceleration' appears in both slots as a distractor. Slot 2 (velocity): 'speed' is the key distractor — momentum is a vector (mass × velocity, direction matters), not mass × speed. Slot 3 (vector): 'scalar' is wrong — scalar quantities have magnitude only. 'derived' and 'base' describe SI quantity categories, not vector/scalar nature. Slot 4 (kg m s⁻¹): 'kg m s⁻²' is the unit of force (F=ma). 'N m' is newton-metre (torque). 'J s' is joule-second (action/Planck's constant) — common misconception from impulse–momentum (impulse N·s = kg m s⁻¹, which is correct but presented as N s not J s).
